claims.hypothesis: Does CO–0.40–0.22 host a compact radio source consistent with an IMBH?
claims.experiment: ALMA Band 6 continuum at 231 and 266 GHz, compared with Sgr A*, submillimetre galaxy counts, and an X-ray limit
claims.result: A point-like source with 8.4 and 9.9 mJy and an inverted spectrum, ~1/500 of Sgr A* luminosity
claims.finding: CO–0.40–0.22* is a promising IMBH candidate

evidence.quote: This point-like continuum source (CO–0.40–0.22$^*$) has a wide-band spectrum consistent with 1/500 of the Galactic SMBH (Sgr A$^*$) in luminosity.

claims.hypothesis: Does a point-mass gravitational kick reproduce the dense clump kinematics?
claims.experiment: N-body simulation with a 10^5 Msun point mass
claims.result: Simulated cloud reproduces the bulk kinematics and the clump spatial-velocity behaviour

evidence.quote: Numerical simulations around a point-like massive object reproduce the kinematics of dense molecular gas well

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thermal dust emission rejected (T~9 K too low); background submillimetre galaxy rejected (~0.1% chance); stellar cluster disfavoured by no IR counterpart

evidence.quote: Thus, the thermal origin of millimetre-wave emission from CO–0.40–0.22$^*$ is implausible.
Non-detection of an infrared counterpart disfavours the stellar cluster interpretation

referee_caveats_inferred: Spectral index from only two close frequencies with large error
Flux values in different beams/epochs combined without variability check
Simulation parameters tuned by hand; uniqueness not tested
Low-temperature thermal and submillimetre galaxy alternatives rely on rough probabilities
Assumes the continuum is associated with an IMBH rather than e.g. a protostar or pulsar
